DIFFERENT QUESTIONS with a byte-identical hash — the case this guard exists for. Both stems read 'The given graph illustrates :' over the same four option TEXTS (the hash sorts options, so the different printed order does not separate them) and both key (A). But 65/7/1's graph is tan^-1 and 65/7/3's is sec^-1, so (A) denotes a different function in each. Committing both would drop one and leave the survivor's key attached to the wrong graph.
collisions.action: HELD OUT of the commit. 65/7/1's row stands; 65/7/3's Q1 is absent from the bank. Revisit at the figure phase: once each row carries its own image_url the two can be told apart by a reader, but they will STILL collide on content_hash, so representing both needs a decision (distinct stems referencing their figures, or accepting one).
collisions.confirmedIndependently: CONFIRMED 2026-08-21 by a second, unrelated method. The figure phase crops every member of a content_hash group and compares them perceptually; across all 41 groups the worst GENUINE reprint measures Hamming 8, and this pair measures 42. Nothing lands between. So the adjudication below - made by reading the two graphs - is corroborated by an image measurement that never read the stems.
collisions.resolution: SETTLED: 65/7/3 Q1 stays out, and the survivor is now BETTER than it was. Representing both is not available without changing contentHash, which sorts option texts and keys on the answer LETTER, so the two are identical to it by construction (see the SUGGESTIONS.md backfill ledger - a bank-wide re-hash of ~38,000 MCQs is not a change to make for one question). Everything cheaper fails too: `context` does not feed the MCQ hash, `source_file` is not in the unique key, and editing the stem would make the transcription unfaithful. Meanwhile the surviving row - cbse-12-pyq-2025-65-7-1, key (A) y = tan^-1 x - now carries its own arctan graph, so the question that WAS unanswerable (a stem naming no function, with no figure) is answerable and self-consistent. Cost: one question of 1,766.
